API reference¶

Flask routes¶

Dynamic Flask analysis page backed by the SQLAlchemy Applicant model.

app.create_app(test_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None) → Flask¶

Create a configurable Flask application without opening a connection.

Tests can replace SESSION_FACTORY, ANALYSIS_RUNNER, and SCRAPE_MANAGER with deterministic doubles. Production uses the Module 3 PostgreSQL and scraper implementations by default.

Parameters:

test_config – Optional overrides applied after the default settings.

Returns:

A Flask application with analysis and background-scrape routes.

app.prepare_analysis(results: dict[str, Any]) → dict[str, Any]¶

Convert ORM values to the assignment’s display formats.

Parameters:

results – Complete ORM result mapping including total_rows and question_1 through question_11. The input is not modified.

Returns:

Template-ready counts, percentages, grouped rows, and a timestamp. Missing numeric averages are represented by the string N/A.

Scraping¶

Collect permitted GradCafe results or import saved browser HTML.

class scrape.GradCafeScraper(output: str | Path = 'applicant_data.json', raw_dir: str | Path = 'raw', delay: float = 6.0, timeout: float = 30.0)¶

Checkpoint collection progress and stop on rejected requests.

Instances are intended for one collection worker, not concurrent access.

output¶

Aggregate applicant JSON path.

raw_dir¶

Directory holding original HTML and per-page journals.

delay¶

Minimum interval between request starts, in seconds.

timeout¶

Network timeout in seconds.

state_path¶

Durable checkpoint JSON path.

robots¶

Loaded robots policy, or None before validation.

last_request¶

Monotonic time of the latest request start.

state¶

Progress, pagination, schema version, and saved stop reason.

records¶

Applicant records committed or recovered from journals.

seen¶

Source URLs already included in records.

check_robots(saved_file: Path | None = None) → None¶

Fetch robots.txt or inspect an explicitly supplied browser copy.

Parameters:

saved_file – Optional saved public policy; otherwise request it.

Raises:

ScrapingStopped – The policy is unreadable or denies results.

ensure_live_allowed() → None¶

Refuse new live operations after a saved rejection or block.

Offline replay into separate paths remains possible. This method never clears the saved stop or treats a browser transport as authorization.

Raises:

ScrapingStopped – A previous stop reason is still recorded.

ingest(payload: bytes, page: int, source_url: str | None = None, method: str = 'urllib') → int¶

Commit one source page and append previously unseen applicants.

Parameters:

  • payload – Original source HTML bytes.

  • page – Sequential capture number, starting at one.

  • source_url – Actual page URL; legacy callers may omit it.

  • method – Human-readable acquisition method for the manifest.

Returns:

Number of newly added records.

Raises:

ScrapingStopped – Policy, identity, or pagination checks fail.

static next_url(html: str, page_url: str) → str | None¶

Find the site’s actual Next link, including cursor pagination.

Parameters:

  • html – Captured source HTML.

  • page_url – The source page’s absolute URL.

Returns:

An absolute Next URL, or None when no link exists.

parse_html(html: str, page_url: str) → list[dict]¶

Extract applicants from a visible public results table.

Parameters:

  • html – Source HTML captured from the public page.

  • page_url – Actual source URL, including any cursor.

Returns:

Clean applicant dictionaries retaining their raw source text.

Raises:

ScrapingStopped – The page is blocked or has an unknown layout.

record_stop(reason: str) → None¶

Persist a stop reason so a blocked live run cannot retry itself.

Parameters:

reason – The rejection or error that stopped the collector.

resolve_atomic_save_stop(resolution: str) → None¶

Clear a reviewed Windows lock on this collection’s output file.

The saved temporary-file replacement pattern must name the configured output on both sides. Website, parser, policy, and general filesystem failures cannot be cleared through this recovery path.

Parameters:

resolution – Nonblank evidence describing the reviewed file lock.

Raises:

  • ValueError – The saved failure is not the supported lock pattern, or the review evidence is blank.

  • OSError – The updated checkpoint cannot be saved.

resolve_browser_transport_stop(resolution: str) → None¶

Clear a reviewed local Chrome connection failure only.

This recovery is intentionally limited to Windows error 10054 and the WebSocket client’s exact remote-host-loss message. Both indicate that the local Chrome DevTools socket closed. HTTP errors, access challenges, rate limits, policy stops, and other failures must remain blocking.

Parameters:

resolution – Human-readable evidence supporting the reviewed retry.

Raises:

ValueError – The saved stop is not the recognized transport error, or no review evidence was supplied.

resolve_parser_stop(resolution: str) → None¶

Clear only a reviewed parser-layout stop after offline validation.

Access denials, challenges, rate limits, and transport failures cannot be cleared through this method.

Parameters:

resolution – Human-readable account of the offline parser review.

Raises:

  • ValueError – The saved stop is not a parser-layout stop.

  • OSError – The updated checkpoint cannot be saved.

scrape_data(target: int = 30000, max_pages: int = 5000) → list[dict]¶

Collect permitted pages until the target or a stop is reached.

Parameters:

  • target – Minimum desired number of unique applicant records.

  • max_pages – Maximum sequential captures to consider.

Returns:

All committed applicant records, possibly below the target.

exception scrape.ScrapingStopped¶

A restriction, unexpected response, or unsafe page stops collection.

scrape.load_data(filename: str | Path = 'applicant_data.json') → list[dict]¶

Load a validated JSON array of applicant dictionaries.

Parameters:

filename – Input JSON path.

Returns:

Applicant records without modifying source values.

scrape.main() → int¶

Run the collection CLI and return its completion/error exit code.

scrape.result_url(page: int) → str¶

Construct a legacy page URL; live collection follows actual Next links.

Parameters:

page – Positive legacy page number.

Returns:

A public HTTPS GradCafe survey URL.

scrape.save_data(data: list[dict], filename: str | Path = 'applicant_data.json') → None¶

Atomically save applicant records to a UTF-8 JSON array.

Parameters:

  • data – Applicant dictionaries to serialize.

  • filename – Destination path relative to the working directory.

scrape.scrape_data(**kwargs) → list[dict]¶

Collect using default files and keyword target/max_pages arguments.

Parameters:

**kwargs – target and/or max_pages forwarded to the scraper method.

Returns:

Committed applicant dictionaries, which may be below the target.

Raises:

  • ScrapingStopped – Policy or response validation stops collection.

  • ValueError – A checkpoint or parsed record is incompatible.

  • OSError – Collection evidence cannot be persisted.

scrape.validate_public_url(url: str) → str¶

Validate a public results or robots URL and remove its fragment.

Parameters:

url – Absolute URL to inspect.

Returns:

The validated URL without a fragment.

Raises:

ScrapingStopped – The URL leaves the permitted public site paths.

Cleaning¶

Clean source text and invoke the instructor’s local LLM package.

clean.clean_data(records: list[dict]) → list[dict]¶

Clean presentation without inferring dates, scores, or outcomes.

Parameters:

records – Extracted applicant dictionaries, including raw fields.

Returns:

New dictionaries with consistent missing values and numeric scores.

clean.extend_with_llm(input_path: Path, output_path: Path, package: Path, batch_size: int = 100, python: str = 'C:\\Users\\DNVR\\Documents\\Hopkins\\Modern Software -- EN.605.256\\jhu_software_concepts\\module_5\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe') → int¶

Run the supplied local app in restartable batches.

The package defines model setup and canonical lists. No API or replacement model is selected. Completed batches are cached by input and package hashes, so changing canonical lists invalidates the cache.

Parameters:

  • input_path – Original applicant JSON array.

  • output_path – Destination for records with added standard fields.

  • package – Directory containing the actual instructor app.py.

  • batch_size – Records per restartable local-model invocation.

  • python – Interpreter with the model dependencies installed.

Returns:

Number of standardized applicant records saved.

Raises:

  • FileNotFoundError – The supplied package is absent.

  • ValueError – Input or model output fails validation.

  • RuntimeError – The supplied model process fails.

clean.main() → int¶

Run the local standardization CLI and return an exit code.

clean.text_value(value: object) → str | None¶

Remove markup/entities and normalize display whitespace.

Parameters:

value – A source value, including None for unavailable information.

Returns:

Clean text or None when no text is available.

Loading¶

Load cleaned GradCafe applicant records into PostgreSQL.

Connection settings prefer DB_* variables, with legacy PG* fallbacks; DATABASE_URL overrides those settings. Missing passwords are prompted for without echo only in an interactive terminal. Provisioning requires an administrator role, separate from the restricted Flask application role.

load_data.batches(rows: Sequence[tuple[object, ...]], batch_size: int) → Iterable[Sequence[tuple[object, ...]]]¶

Yield bounded batches for efficient inserts.

Parameters:

  • rows – Ordered normalized tuples ready for parameter binding.

  • batch_size – Positive maximum number of rows in each yielded slice.

Yields:

Consecutive slices of rows, with a possibly shorter final slice.

load_data.connect_database(create_if_missing: bool = False) → Connection¶

Connect directly unless an authorized loader requests provisioning.

DATABASE_URL takes precedence and connects directly without provisioning. Otherwise, environment settings are used and a missing password is requested privately only when standard input is interactive.

Parameters:

create_if_missing – Whether an administrator loader may create a missing database through the postgres maintenance database.

Returns:

An open connection. The caller must commit/rollback and close it.

Raises:

  • RuntimeError – Noninteractive execution has no configured password.

  • ValueError – The configured port is invalid.

  • psycopg.Error – Authentication, connection, or provisioning fails.

load_data.connection_arguments() → dict[str, object]¶

Build non-secret connection settings from the environment.

Returns:

host, port, dbname, and user settings. DB_* takes precedence over PG*; defaults target local gradcafe with the gradcafe_app role.

Raises:

ValueError – The configured port is not an integer.

load_data.first_present(record: dict[str, Any], *keys: str) → object¶

Return the first nonblank value among equivalent source fields.

Parameters:

  • record – Source applicant dictionary, which is not modified.

  • *keys – Equivalent field names in descending order of preference.

Returns:

The first non-None, nonblank value, or None. Zero remains valid.

load_data.load_rows(rows: Sequence[tuple[object, ...]], batch_size: int) → tuple[int, int, int]¶

Create, load, and validate the table in one transaction.

Parameters:

  • rows – Normalized tuples whose order matches COLUMNS.

  • batch_size – Positive maximum number of rows per executemany call.

Returns:

Counts before loading, after loading, and of distinct stored URLs. Existing URL conflicts are ignored rather than overwritten.

Raises:

  • RuntimeError – Configuration or post-insert schema validation fails.

  • psycopg.Error – Provisioning, insertion, or verification fails.

load_data.main() → int¶

Load the input and print a concise, reproducible summary.

load_data.normalize_record(record: dict[str, Any]) → tuple[object, ...]¶

Map one Module 2 object to the required applicants schema.

Parameters:

record – Applicant dictionary; legacy field aliases are accepted.

Returns:

Values ordered exactly as COLUMNS for parameterized insertion. Missing optional fields become None, which psycopg binds as NULL.

Raises:

ValueError – The URL is absent or a date/numeric value is invalid.

load_data.optional_date(value: object) → date | None¶

Convert source dates such as ‘Feb 12, 2026’ to date objects.

Parameters:

value – date, datetime, supported date string, blank string, or None.

Returns:

A date without time information, or None for missing input.

Raises:

ValueError – A nonblank string matches none of DATE_FORMATS.

load_data.optional_float(value: object, field: str) → float | None¶

Convert a supplied numeric value while preserving missing values.

Parameters:

  • value – Numeric source value, blank string, or None.

  • field – Field name included in validation errors.

Returns:

A finite float, or None for a missing or blank input.

Raises:

ValueError – The value is nonnumeric, infinite, or NaN.

load_data.optional_text(value: object) → str | None¶

Return normalized text, using None for missing or blank values.

Parameters:

value – Source field to stringify and strip, or None.

Returns:

Trimmed text, or None when the input is missing or blank.

load_data.parse_args() → Namespace¶

Parse command-line settings that do not contain credentials.

Returns:

Parsed file path and batch size. Invalid CLI syntax exits through argparse before any database operation is attempted.

load_data.prepare_rows(records: Iterable[dict[str, Any]]) → tuple[list[tuple[object, ...]], int]¶

Normalize records and remove repeated source URLs.

Parameters:

records – Iterable of applicant dictionaries to validate.

Returns:

A pair of ordered database rows and the duplicate-URL count. The first record for each URL is retained; input records are unchanged.

Raises:

ValueError – A record is invalid; the error names its 1-based position.

load_data.read_records(filename: Path) → list[dict[str, Any]]¶

Read and validate the top-level JSON document.

Parameters:

filename – UTF-8 JSON input path, optionally with a byte-order mark.

Returns:

Applicant dictionaries in their original document order.

Raises:

  • ValueError – JSON is invalid or is not an array of objects.

  • OSError – The input file cannot be read.

load_data.verify_schema(cursor: Cursor) → int¶

Verify the live table structure, primary key, and URL uniqueness.

Parameters:

cursor – Open cursor with access to applicants and schema metadata.

Returns:

The number of distinct stored URLs after all checks pass.

Raises:

  • RuntimeError – Columns, identity, primary key, or row uniqueness do not match expectations. This checks data uniqueness, not the presence of a separate UNIQUE constraint in metadata.

  • psycopg.Error – A validation query cannot be executed.

Raw SQL queries¶

Answer the eleven analysis questions with bounded PostgreSQL SQL.

query_data.build_lookup_statement(column: str) → Composed¶

Quote an approved column name while keeping values out of SQL text.

Parameters:

column – Exact member of SEARCHABLE_COLUMNS to compare for equality.

Returns:

A composed SELECT with placeholders for the value and row limit.

Raises:

ValueError – The column is not on the application allowlist.

query_data.clamp_limit(requested: object, default: int = 25) → int¶

Constrain a requested row count before it reaches the database.

Parameters:

  • requested – Integer-like row count supplied by the caller.

  • default – Fallback when conversion fails; also clamped to 1-100.

Returns:

An integer between one and MAX_QUERY_LIMIT, inclusive. Invalid and nonfinite inputs use the fallback instead of reaching PostgreSQL.

query_data.fetch_all(cursor: Cursor, query: str) → list[tuple[Any, ...]]¶

Execute one trusted, bounded analysis query and fetch its rows.

Parameters:

  • cursor – Open cursor owned by the caller.

  • query – Developer-owned SQL constant with an explicit result limit.

Returns:

All rows returned by the bounded query, or an empty list.

Raises:

psycopg.Error – Query execution fails.

query_data.fetch_one(cursor: Cursor, query: str) → tuple[Any, ...]¶

Execute a trusted scalar-analysis query and fetch its first row.

Parameters:

  • cursor – Open cursor belonging to the caller’s read-only connection.

  • query – Developer-owned SQL constant with LIMIT 1, not user input.

Returns:

The first result row as a tuple. Additional rows are not checked.

Raises:

  • RuntimeError – The query produces no row.

  • psycopg.Error – Query execution fails.

query_data.lookup_applicants(cursor: Cursor, column: str, value: str, limit: object = 25) → list[tuple[Any, ...]]¶

Run a bounded lookup with separate statement and bound parameters.

Parameters:

  • cursor – Open psycopg cursor; the caller owns its transaction.

  • column – Approved search column, such as program or term.

  • value – Exact search value, treated as data even if it contains SQL.

  • limit – Requested row count, normalized to the inclusive range 1-100.

Returns:

Rows of (p_id, program, status, term), ordered by p_id.

Raises:

  • ValueError – The search column is not allowed.

  • psycopg.Error – PostgreSQL rejects or cannot execute the lookup.

query_data.main() → int¶

Connect, execute the required SQL, and print formatted results.

query_data.print_analysis(results: dict[str, object]) → None¶

Print every result using the assignment’s required formatting.

Parameters:

results – Complete result mapping returned by run_analysis. Counts use thousands separators; missing averages display as N/A.

query_data.print_question(number: int, question: str) → None¶

Print a consistent heading for console and screenshot output.

Parameters:

  • number – Assignment question number to display.

  • question – Human-readable question text, printed without modification.

query_data.run_analysis(connection: Connection) → dict[str, object]¶

Execute Questions 1-11 using handwritten SQL only.

Sets the supplied connection to read-only; the caller closes it and owns the transaction. LIMIT bounds result rows, not aggregate scanning work.

Parameters:

connection – Open connection with no transaction already in progress.

Returns:

question_1 through question_11 mapped to scalars, the four-score tuple for question_3, or grouped row lists for questions 10 and 11.

Raises:

  • RuntimeError – An expected aggregate result row is absent.

  • psycopg.Error – Read-only setup or any query fails.

ORM queries¶

Repeat selected analyses with SQLAlchemy 2.x ORM expressions.

orm_queries.acceptance_percentage()¶

Return a conditional aggregate for accepted-row percentages.

Returns:

An expression computing accepted / total * 100. NULLIF preserves a missing result for empty groups instead of dividing by zero.

orm_queries.original_university_filter()¶

Match the four universities in the original combined program field.

Print ORM results with the same formatting as the raw-SQL output.

results – Selected-question mapping returned by run_analysis.

orm_queries.run_analysis(session: Session) → dict[str, Any]¶

Execute selected analyses through an ORM Session.

Parameters:

session – Open caller-owned session with SELECT access to applicants.

Returns:

Results for questions 1, 4, 5, 8, 9, and 10. Question 10 contains grouped rows; the other entries contain scalar aggregate values.

Raises:

sqlalchemy.exc.SQLAlchemyError – A query cannot be executed.

orm_queries.run_complete_analysis(session: Session) → dict[str, Any]¶

Execute all 11 ORM analyses for the dynamic Flask page.

Parameters:

session – Open caller-owned session. This function neither closes it nor commits its transaction; the caller controls its lifetime.

Returns:

A mapping with question_1 through question_11 and total_rows. The question_3 row has GPA, GRE, verbal, and writing averages; questions 10 and 11 contain grouped row lists. Empty averages may be None.

Raises:

sqlalchemy.exc.SQLAlchemyError – Query execution or row retrieval fails.

orm_queries.runtime_password() → str | None¶

Use configured credentials or request the password through getpass.

Returns:

None when DATABASE_URL supplies connection settings; otherwise the DB_PASSWORD/PGPASSWORD value or an interactively entered password. Noninteractive callers should configure credentials in advance.
